messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: exec-distro@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly rapid readout — wins, risks, asks (6/18)

Morning leadership team — quick snapshot for this week. Keeping it short and action-oriented. Attached: QBR one-pager v2 and a short extract of support logs related to the latency incident.

Wins
- Dedicated rollout: Canary for customer-facing Dedicated cluster completed for 3 tier-1 customers; measured 18% lower p95 than baseline. On track to finish global rollouts by end of month.
- Model profile automation: Runtime now selects quantization profile automatically for 7/10 common architectures — early experiments show ~22% token-cost savings on mixed workloads.
- Support SLA improvement: Tier-1 mean time to acknowledge dropped from 45m to 18m after rotation of on-call schedule and playbook updates.

Risks / Headwinds
1) Multi-region capacity imbalance — EU demand spike last week overloaded an autoscale policy; fallback to lower-cost variant caused elevated latency impacting two customers (not public). Mitigation: Marcus is deploying a sticky-routing patch + temporary capacity reservation; still needs exec sign-off for a 48-hour burst credit.
2) QBR readiness: Two slides in the customer-facing QBR require updated throughput numbers post-quantization; marketing needs finalized figures by Wednesday EOD or deck will be stale.
3) Compliance evidence: A customer (Acme Health) asked for extended audit logs and a summary of KV-cache deletion policies; security will need a short write-up and a scoped log export.

Asks (actionable, owner, due)
- Marcus Lin: Approve 48h burst capacity credit for EU cluster (estimate $22k). Decision by EOD today if we want to prevent further customer-impact. (attachment: support_log_excerpt.csv)
- Laura Bennett: Can you review and sign off on the updated throughput slide numbers by Wed 6/20 3pm PT? Marketing needs the final asset for QBR.
- Jordan Blake: Please coordinate a 30-min ops/customer call with Acme Health (Nora) to confirm evidence scope — target Thu 6/21.

Notes / context
- The latency bump only affected the higher concurrency endpoints — business impact limited to 2 customers who observed increased tail latency; no data exposure.
- We've prepped a rollback plan for the routing change; will only execute if signaled.

Thanks — appreciate quick reads and decisions where flagged.

--
Soojin Lee
VP, Operations | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

Attachments: qbr_one_pager_v2.pdf (summary), support_log_excerpt.csv (latency incident sample)

Thanks Soojin — noted and helpful. Quick replies: 
- I'll review the throughput numbers this afternoon and aim to get final comments to you by 15:00 PT. If I can't sign off, I'll flag precise language edits so marketing can at least mark the slide as "update pending" instead of shipping inaccurate numbers.
- On the EU burst: send me Marcus's cost estimate and the customer impact summary (who, how long). If it's <48h and addresses the immediate throttle, I'm inclined to approve.

Laura

Soojin / Marcus — quick clarifying Q on the EU capacity issue. When you say "fallback to lower-cost variant," are we referring to a model-variant downgrade (quantized variant) or to routing requests to a different region with higher latency? The mitigation approach differs.

If it's a model-variant downgrade, we should consider a short-lived policy to favor exact-match model routing for paid accounts during the QBR window. If it's regional routing, we need to confirm network hop increases and whether CDN edge adjustments would help.

I can join a quick sync in 20m if helpful. Also Jordan to-do: I'll pull the perf comparison for the affected customers and drop into INF-2145.

Thanks all — quick updates and decisions: 

- Marcus: Confirmed this afternoon — the issue was regional routing to a lower-cost variant (not model-quality downgrade). Marcus has put a sticky-routing change in place and requested a 48h burst credit to add temporary reserved capacity in EU for critical customers. Cost estimate: $21,800. Laura, tagging you to approve; if I don't hear back by 18:00 PT I will provision a 24h emergency reserve (cap $11k) to avoid further customer impact.

- Laura: Appreciate you taking the throughput slide — note I included pre/post quant numbers in the attached qbr_one_pager_v2.pdf. If there are language tweaks, please send them by 15:00 PT tomorrow.

- Jordan: Thanks — confirmed it's regional routing. Please add the perf snapshots to INF-2145; Marcus will reference them in the rollback/playbook doc.

- Acme Health (external): Jordan and Vanessa are scheduled to run the evidence call Thursday 6/21 at 10:00 AM PT. Nora Chen from Acme will join; Jordan to lead, Vanessa to take notes and capture evidence items.

Final ask list (updated)
- Laura Bennett: throughput slide sign-off or edits by Wed 6/20 15:00 PT.
- Marcus Lin: deploy sticky-routing patch + reserve credit (48h if approved). Update by 6/18 18:00 PT on whether 48h approved or fallback to 24h emergency reserve.
- Jordan Blake & Vanessa Ortiz: run evidence call with Acme Health Thu 6/21 10:00 AM PT; provide call notes to security and attach to INF-2145.

I'll file a short exec summary for tomorrow's prep packet once I have Laura's final slide and the billing decision. Thanks for the quick turnaround.
